newsitem.title: GERMANY: BMW, Porsche say no plans as yet for F1 engines.
newsitem.headline: BMW, Porsche say no plans as yet for F1 engines.

text.p: German car makers Porsche AG and BMW AG denied a report that they were poised to supply engines for Formula One racing cars, saying they were not yet ready to enter racing's most expensive spectacle.

Germany's highly-regarded Auto Motor und Sport magazine reported in its most recent edition that the two companies were in talks with two of Formula One's most successful teams to make engines by the end of the century.
According to the magazine, Porsche was negotiating with the Benetton team and was studying how to adapt an existing 3.5 litre engine for Formula one racing.
The magazine also said BMW had signed a contract with the world-champion Williams team to build engines for it from 2000 and was even under pressure to get a motor ready by the 1999 season.

Both car makers said there was no truth to the report, saying their is frequent speculation about their participation in Formula One and that they had not made any progress toward joining any racing team.

"We have neither made a decision nor are we in talks with an F1 team," a BMW spokesman said. But he added that the company was thinking generally about entering Formula One at some point in the future.
A Porsche spokesman, noting that the company was only now emerging from financial difficulty and that it had had to lay off staff, said it was too early to think about joining a racing team.
"Its pure rumour," a Porsche spokesman said. "No decisions have been made about Formula One."
At the center of speculation is Renault's decision earlier this year to pull out of Formula One at the end of the 1997 season, leaving both Williams and Benetton without an engine supplier.

The magazine said Porsche would be a good fit with Benetton because the German firm did not want to spend more than 20 million dollars a year in Formula One and that Benetton had a good sponsor base which would cover running costs.

Auto Motor said that one obstacle in talks between the two was that Porsche would not have an engine ready for a couple years and that Benetton would have to come up with another power plant for at least one year.

Analysts have said Mercedes-Benz's decision to re-enter Formula One several years ago has put pressure on other German car makers to follow suit, but stressed that costly as racing is, involvement is only worthwhile if an engine maker is united with one of the top two or three teams.
